3: וכל And does every [use of the word] "everyone" (הכל) indicate [that the action may be performed] ab initio? - [For if you take that position,] it would be difficult for you [to explain all similar instances where הכל is used]. Nor would you be able to say that every [instance indicates that the action is valid] after the fact. And this is what the tanna means to say: "Everyone as to whom the laws of slaughter apply [may slaughter]." For [otherwise], if those who were disqualified from slaughtering [nonetheless] slaughtered, it would come out that their slaughter was valid [after the fact]. [This result would be unacceptable.]

אלא Rather, "Everyone (הכל) may substitute [an unconsecrated animal for a consecrated animal]" (Tem. 1:1) - Can it be [seriously] claimed that this statement is [intended to authorize that] ab initio, one may bring an unconsecrated animal in place of a consecrated animal, and say, "This one is a substitute for that one"?! [Certainly not! Rather,] the "everyone" in [the tractate of] Temurah is explained over there (Tem. 2a:6-8) to include an heir who substitutes the offering of his [deceased] father, and it is taught over there, that one may not substitute with the offering of another.
